summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "add user preferences storage" brief as architectural, ran the clarifying-question sequence, presented a sectioned design, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, surfaced it for review before writing any implementation code, and began implementation planning only after approval.
reasoning: All five criteria are supported by observed screen text, session-log content, and files on disk. The only nuance is ordering: the spec file was written after the in-chat design approval gate but before any implementation code, and it was explicitly surfaced for review ("Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write out the implementation plan"). That matches the skill's architectural path, so I scored criterion 2 as pass while flagging the ordering as an observation.

observations.description: Codex spec review gate produced no verdict: screen reported 'Both lens captures normalized to incomplete (json payload has no terminal verdict)' and 'The installed companion is 0.0.0-stub (a stub build), which returns an empty payload'. The agent handled it gracefully (recorded ungated event 20260917T100717Z-25980-6082) but the gate effectively did nothing this run.

The design approval gate offered 'Approved as designed' whose subtitle said 'I'll write the spec next' — so the committed spec file is written AFTER the in-chat design approval, not before it. A reader of the acceptance criterion 'wrote a spec before presenting the design for approval' could read this ordering as inverted, though the spec was then re-presented for review before any code.
The agent noted 'no config.toml at $CODEX_HOME' so 'Model and reasoning effort unavailable' — environment config for the Codex companion appears incomplete.

The first brainstorming fork asked the human to choose between browser vs Node surface based on repo contents the human may not know; a one-line summary of what each file currently does would help a non-expert answer.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}' in the active rollout jsonl; no code files changed at that point (git status --short showed only '?? docs/' later).

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/
criteria.evidence: Assistant text line 2 of log: '**Path: architectural.** "Preferences storage" names a subsystem this repo doesn't have ... so I'll go through questions → approaches → a sectioned design → a written spec, rather than jumping to code.' File on disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-preferences-storage-design.md ('# User Preferences Storage — Design ... Status: approved (design), not yet implemented').

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-preferences-storage-design.md (not committed). Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write out the implementation plan.' At that moment `git status --short` in the workdir returned only '?? docs/' — no source files created or modified.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Log grep of assistant text for 'bounded' returned only line 95 ('Running the bounded recovery per the gate's incomplete path') — a Codex-gate recovery step, not a classification. A spec file exists on disk under docs/hyperpowers/specs/.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: jq over assistant text messages grepping 'spike' returned no matches (only 'architectural' at line 2 and 'bounded' at line 95). Flow went design → spec → hyperpowers:writing-plans ('Spec approved. Per the brainstorming skill, the next and only step is the writing-plans skill.').
